newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr opens weaker after overnight selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr opens weaker after overnight selling.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened weaker in heavy trading on Thursday at C$1.3992 (US$0.7146) after overseas investors sold the currency in a heavy overnight trading session, traders said.
* They said broad-based profit-taking helped push the unit past stop-loss levels, propelling the Bank of England to intervene and buy Canada dollars in support of the currency.
The overnight slide of the Canada dollar propelled the Bank of England to intervene and buy Canada dollars on behalf of the Bank of Canada in support of the currency.
Traders said the intervention occurred near the C$1.4010 (US$0.7137) level. The currency strengthened following intervention.
They said intervention by the Bank of Canada was expected today if the Canadian dollar made another move to break through C$1.4010 (US$0.7137) level.
"The question is what happens now that the stop-loss targets are out of the way," one trader said.
Analysts said that merchandise trade numbers released this morning by Statistics Canada would do little to prop up the dollar.
StatsCan reported that Canada's February trade surplus rose to C$2.19 billion. A Reuters forecast predicted the trade surplus would jump to C$2.35 billion.

"It's a wet noodle for the currency," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed income analyst with MMS International. "The numbers are a tad supportive, but they could have been much better. A number like C$3 billion would have been much more convincing."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 1.2303 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.2364 marks and dropped to 89.73 yen from Wednesday's 89.87 yen.
